articles.title: WWE reportedly planning big changes for Ivy Nile
articles.excerpt: Here is all you need to know about the reported big changes coming to Ivy Nile's WWE run.
articles.content:
• By Shounak Chakrabarti
  • Published: 2 Sep 2026, 19:30

According to recent reports, WWE’s creative reportedly has big plans for Ivy Nile.

The Creed Brothers of The American Made recently made their WWE NXT return. Shortly after, speculation also emerged about Nile’s potential return to WWE television.

As per a new report from Fightful Select, WWE’s creative could be working toward her return. “Creative sources within WWE claim that there have been plans for Ivy Nile being developed for quite a while that would see a big change for her,” Fightful Select reported.

It was also noted that sources close to them indicated that Nile’s WWE contract is coming close to its expiry date this fall. Although no details about a new deal have been heard, there were “creative plans being discussed in recent months,” which suggested WWE’s interest in retaining her.

WWE signed Nile to a developmental deal after offering her a tryout in 2020. She spent three years in NXT before moving to Monday Night Raw alongside The Creed Brothers. Later, the trio aligned themselves with Chad Gable to form the heel stable of American Made. However, despite their regular presence on RAW, they slowly started fading away after Gable’s injury last year.

Nile’s last WWE match was a win against PJ Vasa on the August 3rd episode of Main Event, while her last match on RAW was in March, 2026.

articles.title: MrBeast, Gemini AI Team Up to Power Next-Level Survival Stunts | iPhone in Canada
articles.excerpt: MrBeast has inked a multi-year partnership with Google to use Gemini AI and Google Health tech in his extreme survival stunts.
articles.content:
Google has announced a major multi-year partnership with Beast Industries, bringing YouTube titan Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, into its artificial intelligence ecosystem.

The collaboration extends well beyond typical brand integration, weaving Google’s Gemini AI models and Google Health platforms directly into the production of MrBeast’s signature, larger-than-life content.

Donaldson, who recently became the first creator to cross 500 million subscribers on YouTube, plans to use Gemini to help orchestrate, execute, and troubleshoot the complex logistics behind his massive production setups.

The partnership formally kicks off on September 5, 2026, with the release of a high-stakes survival video. In the upcoming challenge, MrBeast and his crew will attempt to navigate and survive three of the world’s most hostile climates: a dense jungle, a scorching desert, and the freezing Arctic. Throughout the challenge, the team will rely on Gemini in real time to calculate route navigation, identify local environmental hazards, analyze shifting weather patterns, and manage emergency logistics.

Beyond survival challenges, the collaboration highlights practical health and fitness integration. Future videos will feature the crew utilizing Google Health tools and wearable hardware like the Fitbit Air to track physical readiness, cardio load, and biometric stress levels during grueling physical feats.

In an official announcement, Marvin Chow, Vice President of Consumer and AI Marketing at Google, emphasized that the goal is to show everyday users how frontier AI tools can assist with ambitious real-world goals.

“Jimmy is always pushing the boundaries of what’s possible,” Chow noted. “Now, he’s tapping into Gemini to help him execute wilder concepts, showing his fans how they can use AI to help turn impossibly big ideas into reality. Along the way, he’ll also show how Google Health can support their daily fitness and wellness goals.”

As part of the broader deal, Donaldson will also star in Google’s upcoming global marketing campaign for the Gemini app. The campaign will highlight behind-the-scenes footage of Donaldson using the assistant as a digital co-producer.

articles.title: NVIDIA Rises 4% on Reported $12.9B Hugging Face Deal, Dell Jumps 8% After Guidance Beat
articles.excerpt: NVIDIA and Dell are both surging on separate catalysts today, but the chip sector fund is barely moving, and that split reveals something important about where the real AI buildout money is actually flowing.
articles.content:
NVIDIA and Dell are both surging on separate catalysts today, but the chip sector fund is barely moving, and that split reveals something important about where the real AI buildout money is actually flowing.

Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Two AI infrastructure names are surging on separate company-specific catalysts, and the broader chip fund is barely moving alongside them. The split says today’s buying is concentrated in two names, not a sector-wide bid on the semiconductor complex.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) stock is up 4% to $225.96 midday after Bloomberg reported that the chipmaker is in advanced talks to acquire AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, with roughly another $1 billion potentially going toward employee retention. Bloomberg said an agreement could come as soon as this week, but no final deal has been reached.

Meanwhile, Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock is up 8% to $457.15 after the server maker raised its full-year revenue outlook by roughly $25 billion and posted its largest quarter on record. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 0.2% to $501.28, so a sector-wide AI bid isn’t showing up in the fund.

Dell Guidance Beat Fuels a Record Quarter

Dell reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $46.97 billion, up 57.8% year over year, and adjusted EPS of $7.04. Dell founder Michael Dell said in a post on X that earnings per share rose 273% year over year, and management flagged broadening demand across compute, storage, and networking.

AI-Optimized Servers revenue doubled year over year to $16.4 billion in the quarter, and Dell booked a record $60.9 billion in AI orders. Dell’s traditional server and networking revenue climbed 122% year over year, storage revenue rose 26%, and the client solutions group was up 20%.

Dell’s full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was raised to $192 billion, up roughly $25 billion from the prior outlook, with AI-Optimized Servers revenue guided to $74 billion for the year. Non-GAAP EPS guidance was lifted to $25.50, and Dell exited the quarter with a record $95 billion AI backlog. The Dell founder captured the moment on X: “There’s an old Texas saying I may have just made up … If you keep growing EPS 200%+ y/y something good will happen.”

NVIDIA’s Reported Hugging Face Bid

The Hugging Face report gives NVIDIA a fresh handle on the open-source model layer that sits on top of its GPUs, and it lands on a day when Dell’s guidance is arguing that AI infrastructure spend is still accelerating. That combination is doing most of the work in NVIDIA stock’s move today.

Hugging Face has become a default distribution point for open-source AI models, and folding it into NVIDIA’s stack tightens the connection between the hardware layer and the model layer that runs on it. Nearly all open models run on NVIDIA, so an acquisition would be less about winning developers than locking in a hub where they already live.

NVIDIA has separately guided to 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, well above prior forecasts of 45%. CEO Jensen Huang put the setup plainly on the company’s last call: “AI is now doing productive and useful work. AI is generating profitable tokens.”

Bloomberg’s report remains a scoop rather than a company announcement, so terms and timing can still shift. Neither NVIDIA nor Hugging Face has confirmed the reported figure, and today’s move should be read against a deal that is pending rather than closed.

Server Maker Outruns the Chipmaker

Through Tuesday’s close, Dell stock was up 241% year to date, while NVIDIA stock was up 17% over the same period. That spread cuts against the assumption that NVIDIA is the purest way to own the AI buildout this year, and it reframes Dell as the deployment-layer beneficiary that has captured the most upside.

Our September 1 coverage noted that Dell’s rally had raised the bar going into this report. Adding another 8% on the release says the results cleared that bar, and by a wide margin.

The read-across for NVIDIA is real but secondary. Dell’s $95 billion AI backlog represents future demand that ultimately routes back to NVIDIA silicon, which helps explain why the chipmaker is up on a day whose primary catalyst belongs to a customer rather than the company itself.

What to Watch Next

Traders can watch for whether the concentrated bid in Dell and NVIDIA broadens into the wider chip complex over the next several sessions. If SOXX starts catching up, the story shifts from two company-specific repricings to a sector-wide reflation of AI hardware names.

Investors sizing their exposure to AI infrastructure should consider whether NVIDIA’s dominance narrative still justifies a single-name concentration in their positions, or whether spreading their allocation across the server layer captures more of the actual buildout (we pulled together seven non-chipmaker suppliers powering this buildout in a free report here). The year-to-date gap between Dell and NVIDIA is the argument for the second view, and today’s action did nothing to close it. A moderate weighting on both layers, sized to their conviction on which one captures more margin over time, is the more balanced read for a prudent investor’s allocation.

articles.title: MrBeast will try to survive 'the planet’s most unforgiving landscapes' using Gemini and Fitbit Air in deal with Google
articles.excerpt: Google has struck a deal with MrBeast, the most popular YouTuber, to promote Gemini and Google Health, with one of...
articles.content:
• Google
  • Gemini
  • Google Health
  • Fitbit Air

Google has struck a deal with MrBeast, the most popular YouTuber, to promote Gemini and Google Health, with one of the first partnerships being a challenge in “the planet’s most unforgiving landscapes.”

In a “multi-year partnership” that extends beyond YouTube, Google will work with MrBeast – aka Jimmy Donaldson – to promote Gemini and Google Health. This starts with a video going live on September 5 on the MrBeast channel that will see Jimmy and co racing through the jungle, desert, and the Arctic, relying on Gemini to help guide them through the challenge. Google says the Fitbit Air will also be integrated into an “upcoming challenge” of some kind.

An ad spot about Gemini will also feature Jimmy, showing how the AI assistant can be used to build out the channel’s infamous stunts.

Google explains:

As the first creator to reach 500 million YouTube subscribers, Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, is always pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Now, he’s tapping into Gemini to help him execute wilder concepts, showing his fans how they can use AI to help turn impossibly big ideas into reality. Along the way, he’ll also show how Google Health can support their daily fitness and wellness goals.

First up on September 5 is a new MrBeast video following Jimmy and his crew as they attempt to survive some of the most extreme and treacherous climates on Earth. Teams will race to navigate three of the planet’s most unforgiving landscapes — the jungle, the desert, and the Arctic — using Gemini to help them identify dangers, survive brutal weather changes, and stay one step ahead.

Beyond YouTube, keep an eye out for Jimmy’s upcoming spot in our newly launched Gemini campaign, where he’ll show how he uses the app as a partner to help him pull off the logistics of his signature, larger-than-life stunts. You’ll also see Jimmy integrate Fitbit Air into an upcoming challenge.
